read_sites._what_this_is: Front-end read-site debt, measured 11 Aug 2026 by Agent W. Both numbers may fall and may never rise.
read_sites._why_this_section_exists: The charter and brain/AGENT_BRIEFING.md have said since 8 Aug 2026 that '129 read sites swallow errors as ?? []'. Agent B measured 263 on 11 Aug and it was reported as having doubled under a gate named silent-failures. It had not doubled and the gate was not stale: THIS CHECK HAD NEVER COUNTED THEM. Everything above it scans generated artefacts and has never opened a front-end file. The 129 was a one-off manual count on 8 Aug that nothing ever re-derived. A figure quoted in three governing documents with no check behind it, drifting for three days, is the same class this file exists for, one level up.
read_sites._the_three_numbers: 263 = occurrences of `?? []` (several lines carry two). 233 = LINES containing it. 129 = the retired 8 Aug manual count. All three are true of different questions, which is why the discrepancy looked like a doubling. The documents have been corrected to 263 with the derivation beside it.
read_sites._which_number_matters: Neither. `(rows ?? []).map(...)` on an array already in hand is harmless and there are dozens. The count that costs is unguardedSupabaseReads: 117 of 142 supabase reads bind `data` and never bind `error`, so a permission denial, a dropped view and a statement timeout are indistinguishable from an empty table. Work that number down first; swallowOccurrences will follow it.
read_sites._the_exemplars: BAD: ForensicAuditLedger, App.jsx:9097. []` sits on the ELSE branch of an explicit error check where it can only mean the query succeeded and returned nothing.
